svg.aria-label: How to write પૈસા: 4 parts, પ, ૈ, સ, ા, one after another
svg.title: Writing પૈસા
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: પ, ૈ, સ, ા (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: પ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, પ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ૈ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/7_kai.svg, groups g1 then g2 (strokes g1s0, g2s0): the ai sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; સ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, સ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ા: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/1_ka.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the aa sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source notes on variation: પ: The teaching app animates પ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the high left hook, curls upward and right over that hook, descends the left stem, then sweeps right around the broad lower body and rises into the right shoulder. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the high left hook, left stem, broad lower body, right shoulder, tall right spine, and lower foot, but its printed hook and body are wider and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's hooked-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the hook, stem, body, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently. ૈ: In the template for કૈ, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ૈ is two pen-down runs: the lower flag first, then the upper flag, each from its upper-left tip, arcing right and down to the lower right. t30apps, already cited for ઐ, sweeps the two high arcs in the same order and direction: the lower arc first, then the higher, each from left to right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 76 of its 83 stored prototypes of the ai sign (92%) are two strokes, the left flag first. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. સ: The teaching app animates સ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles the rounded upper loop, descends through the left body, then sweeps across the long right shoulder. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper loop, left body, long right shoulder, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed loop is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, body, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently. ા: In the template for કા, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ા is one pen-down run that starts at the top of the bar, draws it straight down, and ends in a short foot to the right at the baseline. t30apps' Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice, already cited for આ, draws its trailing ā stem the same way: after the body, down into a matching foot. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 55 of its 81 stored prototypes of the aa sign (68%) are one stroke, and 98% of those move downward. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 2 of 4 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Part 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, પ animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 2: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/7_kai.svg, groups g1 then g2
(strokes g1s0, g2s0): the ai sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
Part 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, સ animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 4: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/1_ka.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0):
the aa sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
